2000: The intercom crackled to life, cleared its throat, and told you nothing you could act on.
2001: A calm voice welcomed you aboard by no name in particular, which felt oddly personal anyway.
2002: The crew demonstrated the seatbelt, in case anyone aboard had never met a belt before.
2003: A flight attendant pointed to the exits with both hands, calm as a very gentle traffic officer.
2004: The masks dropped in the demonstration and everyone watched, quietly hoping never to meet one.
2005: A chime rang, and the whole cabin looked around to see who it was for, then decided it was for someone else.
2006: The captain came on to say we were cruising smoothly, which you had, until then, simply assumed.
2007: A crew member mimed blowing a tiny whistle, and the whole cabin nodded as if they'd heard it.
2008: The seatbelt sign dinged off and forty belts unclicked at once, a small orchestra of freedom.
2009: The announcement began in a language you didn't know, and you understood the calm tone perfectly.
2010: The captain's voice was so relaxed you briefly forgot you were sitting inside a machine in the sky.
2011: A crew member walked the aisle checking belts, and you sat up straight like a caught daydreamer.
2012: The intercom asked you to sit back and relax, two things you were already failing at heroically.
2013: The captain listed the cruising speed with great pride, and you were, honestly, a little impressed.
2014: A flight attendant showed the life vest, tugging cords no one at this height wished to ever test.
2015: The seatbelt sign lit up, then off, then on again, running a small private argument with itself.
2016: The crew noted the nearest exit might be behind you, which felt like a small, very gentle threat.
2017: The captain thanked the crew, the crew thanked you, and you thanked no one, having done the least.
2018: An announcement asked everyone to switch off their devices, and the whole cabin quietly disobeyed.
2019: The captain apologized for the short delay so warmly you forgave a whole plane for being a plane.
2020: A flight attendant smiled the exact same calm smile at every row, and yours felt just as sincere.
2021: The intercom clicked on, paused for one long dramatic moment, and then simply said thank you.
2022: The safety demonstration ended and everyone applauded no one, out of habit and mild relief.
2023: The captain announced clear skies ahead in a voice that made clear skies sound like a personal favor.
2024: A flight attendant folded both arms into a single graceful arrow, and the whole cabin obeyed a shape.
2025: The announcement woke you gently to inform you that you should, at some point soon, wake up.
2026: The crew mimed the whole safety routine in perfect sync, a silent little play for a dozing crowd.
2027: The captain gave the local time at our destination, and your inner clock loudly disagreed with all of it.
2028: A chime sounded, a light blinked, and a crew member appeared as if summoned by tiny magic.
2029: The intercom promised a smooth rest of the flight, then seemed to dare the sky to prove it wrong.
2030: The crew came through collecting cups, and you surrendered yours like a small tribute to the sky.
2031: A crew member checked that your tray was stowed, and you felt briefly, wonderfully, responsible.
2032: The seatbelt sign glowed on, and the whole cabin sat a little straighter, obeying a small orange square.
2033: The captain welcomed frequent flyers warmly, and you clapped along, having flown quite a lot lately.
2034: An announcement asked everyone to keep belts fastened while seated, as if anyone planned to wander.
2035: The crew showed how to brace for landing, and you practiced once, quietly, just to feel prepared.
2036: The captain returned to say we'd be on the ground shortly, which is where you very much prefer to be.
2037: A flight attendant pointed out the floor lights, and you felt reassured by glowing dots you hoped never to follow.
2038: The intercom crackled, everyone leaned in to listen, and it was only a soft apology for the noise.
2039: The captain mentioned some bumps ahead so casually you almost admired how little it seemed to worry him.
